function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Iceland isn’t known for a huge professional ice‑hockey scene, but if you’re looking to combine a visit to a lively city with some ice‑hockey action, **Reykjavík** is your best bet. ### Why Reykjavík? | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Largest city & capital** | Reykjavik is the cultural, economic, and sporting hub of Iceland. | | **Ice‑hockey facilities** | • **Laugardalur Ice Rink** – home to the national team’s training and a popular venue for local leagues.
• **Halli 33** – a modern arena that hosts international matches and club games. | | **Events** | • The **Icelandic Hockey League** (Úrvalsdeild karla) plays out here, with teams like **Íshúsfélagið** and **Skautafélag Reykjavíkur** competing.
• International tournaments such as the **Nordic Cup** sometimes feature Reykjavik as a host city. | | **Accessibility** | • Keflavík International Airport connects Reykjavik to major European hubs.
• Public transport (buses, taxis, bike rentals) makes getting around easy. | | **Other attractions** | • Golden Circle tour nearby.
• Blue Lagoon, Hallgrímskirkja church, Harpa concert hall, and vibrant nightlife. | ### How to catch a game 1. **Check the schedule** – The Icelandic Hockey Association’s website lists fixtures for the Úrvalsdeild karla season (usually running from September to March). 2. **Buy tickets** – Most games sell through the rink’s box office or online via the team’s official sites. 3. **Plan your stay** – Book accommodation close to Laugardalur or Halli 33 for convenience. If you’re willing to travel a bit further, **Akureyri** (the “Capital of North Iceland”) also has an active local league and a decent rink, but the overall experience—both in terms of hockey and city life—is richer in Reykjavik. Enjoy the blend of Icelandic culture and the thrill of watching local players compete on the ice!
